vedic_reference.note: The name Jagat is derived from the Sanskrit root word jag, which means to be conscious, to awake. In Hindu mythology, Jagat is the name of the material world, created by the god Brahma. It is often used to refer to the entire universe or the physical world.

data.cultural_impact: The term Jagat has been used in various contexts in Hinduism, particularly in philosophical and religious texts. It represents the cyclic nature of the universe and the interconnectedness of all beings within it. It is also used to signify the vastness and diversity of the material world and the experiences that come with it. In Hindu mythology, there are various gods and goddesses associated with Jagat, including Brahma, who is considered the creator of the universe, and Vishnu, who preserves the cosmic order.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Jagat can be seen as a reminder of the impersonal nature of the universe and the transient quality of all experiences. It represents the illusion of the world and the importance of transcending it through the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and awakening to the ultimate reality of the Self (Atman). Ultimately, the term Jagat emphasizes the interconnectedness of all things and the importance of recognizing the divine presence in all of creation.

historical_references.reference: The Puranas describe Jagat as the physical universe, created by Brahma and governed by Shiva and Vishnu.
In the Mahabharata, the term Jagat is used to refer to the world as opposed to the divine or heavenly realms.
